key_insight: Across perovskites, polar off-centering enhances low-frequency infrared and dielectric responses, while nonpolar octahedral tilting is associated with Raman central peaks.
engineering_relevance: Linking spectral features to lattice instabilities can help interpret structural dynamics in halide-perovskite solar-cell materials, though device-performance gains are not demonstrated.
method: Use machine-learning-based molecular dynamics to simulate infrared and Raman spectra.
Compare seven oxide, halide and double-halide perovskites.
Relate spectral features to instability symmetry, coupling and dynamics.
evidence_signal: Simulations across seven compounds indicate that slow polar reorientations shift dielectric responses to very low frequencies, while overdamped tilting produces persistent Raman central peaks.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative accuracy benchmarks or solar-cell device validation.
paper_title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
